messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated prefix-cache miss rate detected for service=svc-llm-prod-15 in us-west-2. 5m miss_rate=0.42 (baseline 0.03). origin_fetches ↑12x, p99_latency +240ms. Paging oncall-raj. See metrics snapshot: https://metrics.redwood.example/s/svc-llm-prod-15

oncall-raj: acked. I'm awake and looking. please add logs/traces if you have them.

sylvia: I'm on it too. initial thought: could be a cache invalidation job kicked off? last deploy 23:12 UTC. Will check deployment events.

tomas: checking rollout history now. `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> `abc1234` pushed at 23:10 UTC. No scheduled invalidation in CI, but infra cron `prefix-invalidator` ran at 23:14 UTC per cron logs. pulling logs...

maria: heads up — customer-facing alerts: a few customers reported latency spikes and slow responses on chat endpoints around 23:20-23:40 UTC. No 5xxs in initial pass but user-level latency >1s more frequent. Assessing severity.

evam: (note: evoops) typo, meant evan — scaling KV pool to warm nodes now to reduce misses.

oncall-raj: can someone dump the KV hitrate timeline and origin fetch counts? want a short timeline for pager notes.

incident-bot: metrics snapshot link: https://metrics.redwood.example/dash/svc-llm-prod-15?range=30m

sylvia: quick grep of invalidator logs: `grep "prefix-invalidate" /var/log/prefix-invalidator.log | tail -n 50` -> shows a full sweep at 23:14 with ~1.1M keys invalidated. suspicious.

sylvia: timeline so far (local notes):
- 23:03 UTC: normal traffic
- 23:10 UTC: deploy abc1234 (config change: `cache.eviction.batch_size` from 100 -> 1000)
- 23:14 UTC: prefix-invalidator cron executed; large sweep (~1.1M keys)
- 23:18 UTC: KV hit-rate begins to drop (dash shows drop from 0.95 -> 0.53 in 5m)
- 23:22 UTC: origin fetches spike, p99 latency increases
- 23:26 UTC: pager triggered

oncall-raj: good timeline. hypothesis A: the deploy increased eviction aggressiveness (batch_size) which coupled with the invalidator sweep caused mass invalidation and downstream rewarm storm. Hypothesis B: invalidator bug (regex matches too broad) — need sample of invalidator job args.

maria: customer impact summary (brief): several mid-market customers using chat endpoints saw L1 latency climbs and a handful reported degraded UX. No confirmed request failures. We should prepare comms if this persists >1hr.

evan: I'm starting a targeted mitigation: throttle invalidator and scale up warm pool nodes. Commands:
```
# throttle invalidator immediate
sudo systemctl stop prefix-invalidator || true
kubectl scale deployment svc-llm-warm-pool --replicas=8 -n prod
```
I'll run now, report back.

devops-bot: action executed: `systemctl stop prefix-invalidator` on infra-03 (success). Warm pool scale started (desired=8, current=3).

oncall-raj: thanks. sylvia, can you pull a sample of origin request logs for 23:14-23:26 and share a few trace ids? want to see if single key patterns dominate.

sylvia: sharing logs: https://logs.redwood.example/abcd1234 (filtered for origin_fetch). sample traces: trace/0x7a1, trace/0x7a2, trace/0x7b0. Observed lots of prefix lookups for short prefixes like `the ` and `user:` — suggests broad invalidation.

tomas: I inspected the deploy diff. The change to `cache.eviction.batch_size` was intentional for mempressure, but the invalidator cron uses a separate regex in `scripts/prefix_invalidator.py`. Recent change in repo (PR #432) accidentally widened match from `^user:` to `^.*:` when a variable interpolation failed. blame -> commit `def456`. That commit was merged at 23:08 UTC. PR author is infra-eng-squads; tagging them.

maria: tagging @support-leads to prepare for possible customer comms. Also pinging account execs for the affected customers.

oncall-raj: immediate plan: 1) stop invalidator (done), 2) roll back commit def456 to restore regex, 3) scale warm pool until hit-rate recovers, 4) monitor p99 and origin fetches. Who will roll back?

tomas: I'm rolling back the faulty commit now. `git revert def456 --no-edit && ./deploy.sh svc-llm-prod-15`

devops-bot: deploy started for svc-llm-prod-15 (revert def456). CI artifacts ok.

incident-bot: metric alert update: miss_rate now 0.31 (down from 0.42) after invalidator stopped and warm pool scaling started. Origin fetches dropped ~40% in last 6 minutes.

sylvia: confirming logs — origin fetch rate trending down. KV hit-rate climbing back toward 0.82. still below baseline but improving.

maria: customer impact update: some customers report partial recovery in latency; open support tickets updated. No escalations yet.

oncall-raj: good. capturing timeline + actions for RCA. Please paste full commands/links used during mitigation into this thread for handoff.

evan: Mitigation commands used:
```
sudo systemctl stop prefix-invalidator
kubectl scale deployment svc-llm-warm-pool --replicas=8 -n prod
git revert def456 --no-edit
./deploy.sh svc-llm-prod-15
```
All executed between 23:28-23:36 UTC.

incident-bot: snapshot: p99 latency delta down to +60ms over baseline, miss_rate 0.15 after 10m. Suggest clearing alert once stable for 15m.

tomas: rolling retention of invalidation job until PR fix lands. I'll open follow-up PR to add unit tests for regex and a safety cap on invalidation set size. Ticket: INF-789.

sylvia: logs and grep snippets saved here: https://logs.redwood.example/session/1952109876 (includes `grep "prefix-invalidate" outputs and origin fetch samples)

maria: comms note: prepping a short message for affected customers explaining transient latency due to cache rewarm after invalidator run; will coordinate with trust & safety/account teams.

oncall-raj: thanks team. I'm going to handoff to the next oncall in 40m. Summary for handoff (paste into rotation):
- Incident type: prefix cache mass invalidation -> KV miss storm -> increased origin fetches -> p99 latency spike
- Root cause (prelim): faulty invalidator regex introduced by commit def456 + concurrent change that increased eviction aggressiveness (abc1234) caused broad invalidation sweep
- Actions taken: stopped invalidator, scaled warm pool, reverted def456, redeployed (timestamps + commands in thread)
- Current state: hit-rate recovering (0.82 -> 0.90), p99 close to baseline, origin fetches decreasing.
- Follow-ups: INF-789 (unit tests + safety cap), postmortem doc, customer comms draft.

devops-bot: note: autoscaling logs show warm pool scaling completed at 23:33 UTC, replicas=8.

oncall-raj: assigning the RCA write-up to sylvia/tomas, comms to maria. I'll add incident tag and start a postmortem doc template.

sylvia: will take RCA write-up. I'll include timeline, logs, sample traces, and a fix diff + test plan.

tomas: adding INF-789 and PR to infra repo. planning to add an opt-in kill-switch for large invalidation sweeps.

maria: will prepare customer comms draft and share in #customer-comm for review.

oncall-raj: handing off to next oncall @dev-rotation. Please monitor the metrics for the next 2 hours and escalate if miss_rate > 0.2 or p99 > +200ms.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident moved to "mitigated" state by oncall-raj at 23:44 UTC. Recording timeline and participants.

maria: quick note for RCA: include quant numbers — peak origin fetch rate 12x baseline, keys invalidated ~1.1M, time to recovery ~17m from mitigation start.

sylvia: will include those metrics and attach log export. finishing initial RCA draft and will link here when done.

oncall-raj: thanks everyone. closing loop with oncall handoff.
